text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ontario health minister resigns: Probe called into aide's handling of medical files; Wilson denies knowledge of it.
- Prime Minister cool to vote on distinct society: Chretien retreats on earlier vow.
- Organizers of Serb protests play to Western television: Students hope to bring foreign pressure on Milosevic.
- Internet porn results in arrest: Ottawa scientist faces charges.
- Quebec unions threaten chaos: Bouchard warned not to reject counterproposal from public-sector workers.
- New home building heats up: As housing starts post 17 percent gain in November, builders harken back to boom of 1980s.
- Stock markets roar back: Yesterday's gains offset Friday's selloff.
- General Motors churning out muscle cars: Ste-Therese working overtime despite 6-month stockpile.
- Ault Foods sells ice cream business: Nestle subsidiary to pay $221 million.
- WIC's power elite challenged: U.S. arbitrager picks a fight, trying to break the grip of media company's controlling Griffiths family, and seeking a breakup of WIC's assets.
- Newbridge employee charged with selling company assets.
